claims.reason: Box heading is 'patient exposed to infectious fluid'. 'Body fluid' is deliberately broader (it also covers the tears/saliva/sweat/urine/stool the intro calls non-infectious), which is acceptable for a task trigger since the check_for then narrows to the page's list; every listed fluid is_a Body fluid so descendant matching works. No usable closer concept: 'Exposure to blood and/or body fluid' is an event, not a finding/substance pair.

claims.rule: Check for HIV PEP: exposure to infectious fluid or human bite
Check for HIV PEP: exposure to infectious fluid or human bite
claims.reason: The page's item is 'Human bite severe enough to cause bleeding': bleeding caused by the bite. A bare 'Bleeding' finding is any bleeding anywhere (e.g. a nosebleed recorded on another page) and is only tied to the bite by the and in the priority rule, so a patient with a trivial human bite plus unrelated bleeding becomes Urgent. No precoordinated 'bleeding human bite' concept exists.
claims.fix: Record the severity on the bite itself: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Human bite - wound" "disorder") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Severe (severity modifier)" "qualifier value"))), and use that single qualified finding in the priority rule; or keep Bleeding but document the approximation.

rules.rule: Check for HIV PEP: exposure to infectious fluid or human bite
rules.problem: Type and trigger are right, but the check_for is incomplete against the red box and its follow-on question. (1) The box's first bullet also lists 'blood-stained fluid/tissue'; nothing encodes it and 'Exposure to Blood' does not match it by descent, so no SNOMED pairing is attempted (no precoordinated concept exists; a remaining-questions note or an approximation such as a second Blood exposure finding with a documented caveat is needed). (2) The page's next triage step, 'Yes: was there sexual contact, sharps injury, splash to eye/open wound/mouth/nose?', is the gate that separates the PEP pathway from 'for all other exposures, reassure ... avoid giving PEP'; it is not checked for although (snomed_concept "Sharps injury" "disorder") and (snomed_concept "Sexual exposure" "finding") exist. (3) 'Bleeding' is unlinked to the bite (c013).

rules.rule: Urgent: HIV PEP, exposure to infectious fluid or bleeding human bite
rules.problem: Type and level are right: the box heading is 'Give urgent attention to the patient exposed to infectious fluid. Does patient have either of:', so Urgent on an or of the two bullets is faithful, and the bite bullet is correctly an and of bite plus bleeding. Two gaps: exposure to blood-stained fluid/tissue (explicitly in the box) never triggers Urgent, and the bare Bleeding finding lets an unrelated bleed plus any human bite trigger it (c025). Every piece of evidence is checked for in the same file.

summary: Nothing is invented and every concept exists; the red box's eleven items are encoded with the right concepts and the Urgent level matches the heading. The most consequential gap is that 'blood-stained fluid/tissue', an explicit red-box item, is encoded nowhere, so such an exposure is neither checked for nor made Urgent. Secondary: the bare 'Bleeding' finding is not tied to the human bite, and the page's second triage question (sexual contact / sharps injury / splash to eye, open wound, mouth or nose), which decides PEP versus reassurance, is not checked for even though SNOMED has Sharps injury and Sexual exposure.
